title: The Reeds' carcasses are barebone tentacles that crumble from the tips with time and break apart under fire
context: Owner, 2026-10-10: "the low-poly reeds carcasses are too low poly, they look blocky. can we have them more simple renditions of tentacles? barebone tentacles, and they disintegrate with further explosions or time." Follows 2026-10-10-boss-bait-wave-emergence-120hz-carcasses, whose carcass was the tet cage's outer surface in the collapsed pose, flat shaded (1,584 triangles), darkening, flattening and sinking over 60 s. The kit (src/fx/nih-dairia/*), src/sentry-pilot.js and the game's src/fx/* are untouched.
outcome: THE LIMB CHAINS: the kit stores no limb-to-node map; its own limb rule (src/fx/nih-dairia/limb-separation.js) sorts the rest nodes by their distance from the axis (the torso within 0.022 native units, a limb from 0.035) and their sector (the nearest of limbCount directions). src/domain/boss-carcass.js `limbRings` applies the same rule (a limb from 0.03 so the chain starts at the shoulder) and cuts each limb into 10 equal bands of rest distance, root to tip: on the Reed's cage, 4 limbs of 10 rings (173-175 nodes each) round 111 torso nodes. THE SHAPE (src/labs/boss/carcass.js): at the lay-down (unchanged: corpse 2 s and the collapse settled), each ring's centre in the collapsed pose, smoothed (two 1-2-1 passes), a centripetal Catmull-Rom curve from half-way into the torso through them; a tube of 8 sides, smooth shaded, its radius 0.6 of twice the ring's smaller principal deviation across the curve (the limbs are flatter than wide: the full spread read as fat pipes) under a taper to 0.1 of the root's (power 1.2); cut into 8 pieces of 3 rings, each capped; a 10x8 ellipsoid on the torso's spread as the core. One merged geometry and one MeshStandardMaterial a carcass, the skin's mean colour x0.72, in the Reed's own drawing frame: 2,188 triangles (33 pieces). THE DISINTEGRATION: `crumbleTimes` gives each limb's pieces seeded times from its tip inward between 15 % and 90 % of the 60 s decay (a piece never before the one beyond it; the core goes with the carcass); its time come, a piece shrinks and sags over 1.2 s and leaves the index. Every round the fight resolves (wave.resolve: the 25 mm stream's rounds, the 40 mm and MK-9 landings, also once the boss is in) is taken through the sphere into each carcass's own frame (a re-anchor never moves a carcass, and on the lab's 750 m planet a shifted local point drifts by metres after a few re-anchors) and `blastBreaks` takes the whole or crumbling pieces within the break radius, nearest first: the 25 mm at most 3 within 3 m, the 40 mm every one within 8 m (its 22 m damage radius would take a whole carcass), the MK-9 every one in its 55 m ring. A broken piece is thrown outward from the impact at 18 m/s (faster nearer) and up at 12 m/s under 30 m/s2, tumbling, whole for 40 % of its 0.8 s and then shrinking to nothing. COST: an untouched carcass is a colour, an emissive and a sink a frame as before plus one look at its next crumble time; only moving pieces have their vertices rewritten (from a rest copy), the index is rebuilt only when a piece goes. The carcasses no longer flatten (a squashed tube reads wrong); they darken, sink and cool as before, at most 30. The readout's wave line logs the carcasses, their ms and the pieces moving (0.0-0.2 ms with 20 lying). The handle's wave() carries each carcass's limbs and pieces (state, why it went, local point now), its blasts, the stats and the last blast; closeTo(id) puts the free orbit's camera on one.
alternatives: Separate meshes per piece (rejected: 20 Reeds x 33 pieces is 660 draw calls; one merged geometry with an index rebuilt on removal is one a carcass)
An InstancedMesh of straight tapered cylinders (rejected: a straight piece kinks at every joint; the merged tube follows the curve)

A per-piece offset attribute and a shader patch (rejected: the seat's thermal and the heat tagging read the materials as they are; a CPU rewrite of the few moving pieces costs nothing while nothing moves)
The rings' full spread for the radius (tried: fat octagonal pipes at the root, still blocky close up; the thinner axis is the barebone)
The fight's own damage radius for the 40 mm break (rejected: 22 m takes a whole 15 m carcass; the owner's 'disintegrate' reads better a limb or two at a time, and the test needs the others left)
Shifting the pieces' local points with each re-anchor (tried first: the suite's 40 mm aimed at a carcass after ten re-anchors missed; the impact is now taken into the carcass's own frame)
evidence: node --check on every edited file; npm test (229 programs; test/boss-carcass.mjs new: the Reed's cage read from its asset into 4 limbs of 10 rings in their sectors root to tip, the crumble seeded and tip-first per limb, every tip before any root, the core never, the breaks per gun within the radius nearest first capped, a piece already gone not broken again, the throw outward and up and whole for its first part, the decay; carcassLook moved there from boss-wave.js), npm run check, npm run build green

from a snapshot, sequentially, one headless Chrome (memory WARN on pinned swap, ~31 % headroom): --boss-wave green (extended): the first carcass 4 limbs of 8 pieces round a core, 2,188 triangles; a 40 mm round aimed at a fresh carcass's limb tip broke 22 pieces 1.3-7.9 m from the landing and left 7 whole (the nearest 8.5 m off), 38 pieces moving, the flown ones gone after; time crumbled 112 pieces across 20 carcasses with none out of tip-first order; the shortened decay darkened, cooled and sank them and they went; --boss-friends green, --boss green

screenshots (scratchpad): carcass-close.png (the free orbit 12 m off: curved tapered tentacles round a smooth core, crumbled tips cut flat), carcass-tentacles.png (the seat zoomed x5 in the thermal: the warm carcasses read as thin-armed starfish shapes beside the boss; cold ones fade into the ground), carcass-blast.png (the 40 mm's burst on a carcass; the thrown pieces are a few pixels at 430 m)
